elements.element: Vendor has a duty to defend.
elements.evidence: MSL expressly agrees to “defend” IBM.

elements.element: Vendor has a duty to indemnify and hold harmless.
elements.evidence: MSL expressly agrees to “hold harmless, and indemnify” IBM against claims, damages, liabilities, losses, and expenses.

elements.element: Customer is a covered indemnified party.
elements.evidence: IBM, the Customer, is the express beneficiary of MSL’s obligations.

elements.element: Customer affiliates are covered indemnified parties.
elements.evidence: The clause names only IBM and does not extend protection to IBM’s affiliates.

elements.element: The Vendor duties cover third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The clause covers “any and all claims,” and the exclusions expressly refer to “such third party claim.”

elements.element: The Vendor duties cover claims alleging that the services infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Coverage includes infringement by MSL “in rendering performance under this Agreement” across an enumerated range of intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor duties cover claims alleging that deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Coverage expressly includes MSL-procured designs, deliverables, materials, and Products.

elements.element: The Vendor duties cover claims arising from Vendor’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: No indemnity trigger addresses MSL’s breach of law.

elements.element: The Vendor duties cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No data-breach indemnity trigger appears.

elements.element: The Vendor duties cover claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is not an indemnity trigger.

elements.element: The Vendor duties cover claims arising from Vendor’s wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is not an indemnity trigger.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of covered claims.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no claim-notice procedure.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure addresses control of the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: The clause does not allocate control of the defense or settlement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires Customer’s reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no cooperation obligation.

elements.element: Any content-based Customer indemnity applies only to content provided by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no indemnity obligation on IBM, so no broader content-based Customer indemnity exists.

elements.element: Any law-based Customer indemnity applies only to Customer’s own breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no indemnity obligation on IBM, so no broader law-based Customer indemnity exists.

elements.element: Customer has no indemnity obligation for grounds other than Customer-provided content or Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: No IBM indemnity obligation is included at all; therefore IBM is not obligated on any additional ground.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property infringement claims.
elements.evidence: MSL must defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM for infringement claims, and the clause expressly characterizes the relevant claims as third-party claims.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity covers infringement arising from the services.
elements.evidence: The indemnity covers infringement by MSL “in rendering performance under this Agreement.”

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity covers infringement arising from deliverables.
elements.evidence: The indemnity expressly covers MSL-procured designs, deliverables, materials, Parts, and Products.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: There is no exclusion for modifications made by IBM.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: There is no exclusion for combinations with other products, systems, materials, or services.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: The clause excludes claims caused by MSL’s material compliance with written IBM specifications and defective designs resulting from IBM specifications or designs.

elements.element: The IP cure regime is mandatory and performed at Vendor’s expense.
elements.evidence: The redline changes the remedy to “MSL shall, at its own expense” provide one of the stated cures.

elements.element: The IP remedies include procuring necessary rights or licenses.
elements.evidence: MSL must have the option to “procure any necessary license rights.”

elements.element: The IP remedies include modifying the affected item to make it non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The option to use non-infringing designs and processes while maintaining contractual specifications functionally provides a modification remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies include replacing the affected item with a non-infringing substitute.
elements.evidence: The clause permits use of non-infringing Parts, deliverables, or other materials and expressly refers to them as “substitute items.”

elements.element: The IP remedies require a refund if procurement, modification, and replacement are unavailable.
elements.evidence: If none of the preceding remedies is available, MSL must refund the fees paid for the affected Products.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity is carved out of the general liability cap.
elements.evidence: The general cap begins with an express exception for MSL’s Section 15.1 indemnification obligations.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section 15.1 indemnification obligations are expressly limited to “three times (3X) the annual fees paid to MSL under this Agreement.”

result.reason: The redline makes the cure regime mandatory, adds a fallback refund, and replaces application of the general cap with a 3× annual-fees super-cap. It nevertheless fails the fallback because it omits the usual Customer-modification and combination exclusions. It also falls well short of the preferred position by omitting affiliate coverage, non-IP indemnity triggers, and notice/control/cooperation procedures. The edits are targeted and preserve unrelated commercial terms, but drafting quality is reduced by duplicate subsection lettering, stray punctuation, and some ambiguity in the annual-fees measure.
